map.压力知觉量表(PSS-10)是国际通用的压力评估工具，10题评估过去1个月内对生: The Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) is an internationally used stress assessment tool. Its 10 items evaluate how stressful life has felt over the past month, 0-4 points each, for a total of 0-40.
map.PSS-10（压力知觉量表）共 10 题，评估「过去 1 个月」的压力感知。每题: PSS-10 (Perceived Stress Scale) has 10 items assessing perceived stress over the "past 1 month". Each item is rated 0-4 by frequency (0 = never, 1 = occasionally, 2 = sometimes, 3 = fairly often, 4 = very often). Items 4, 5, 7 and 8 are reverse-scored (choosing 4 records 0, 3 records 1, 2 records 2, 1 records 3, 0 records 4, flipped automatically). Adding the 10 items gives a total of 0-40: 0-13 low stress, 14-19 moderate/normal, 20-26 fairly high, 27-40 high stress. Everything runs in the browser and no answer is uploaded.

map.10 题中第 4、5、7、8 题为反向计分题，系统会自动翻转，请按真实感受作答: Items 4, 5, 7 and 8 of the 10 are reverse-scored and the system flips them for you, so answer with your genuine feeling
map.每题 5 档从「从不」到「很频繁」，拿不准就选最接近的一档: Each question has 5 levels from "never" to "very often"; if unsure, pick the closest one

map.工作负荷自查：连续加班、 deadline 密集时，用它确认「不可控感」是否已经: Workload self-check: when overtime runs back to back and deadlines pile up, use this to confirm whether your sense of loss of control has climbed and plan rest ahead of time.
map.考试 / 项目前：大考前或项目冲刺期测一次，区分「适度紧张」与「长期高压」，避免: Before an exam or project: measure once before a big exam or during a project sprint to tell "healthy tension" apart from "sustained high pressure" instead of pushing through blindly.
map.慢性压力跟踪：每月固定自测，观察总分走向，判断生活节奏是否失衡。: Chronic stress tracking: run it at a fixed time each month and watch the trend of the total to judge whether your life rhythm is out of balance.
map.第 4、5、7、8 题是反向计分：你越觉得「能掌控、能从容应对」，反而得分越低。: Items 4, 5, 7 and 8 are reverse-scored: the more you feel you "can stay in control and cope calmly", the lower the score. This cancels out blind optimism so the total reflects your real stress more closely.
map.PSS 测的是压力事件还是压力感受？: Does PSS measure stressful events or the feeling of stress?
map.它测的是「你对过去一个月压力的主观感受与失控感，而非客观事件数量」。同样的事，不: It measures "your subjective sense of stress and loss of control over the past month, not the number of objective events". The same event feels very different to different people.
map.分数高就一定需要就医吗？: Does a high score always mean I need medical help?
map.不一定。高分提示压力偏大、需要调节；但若伴随持续失眠、情绪崩溃或躯体不适，建议寻: Not necessarily. A high score means stress is on the high side and needs managing; but if it comes with persistent insomnia, emotional breakdown or physical discomfort, seek professional help.
